sets.q: Lesson 4 review. 3.5 × 2.6 = ____
sets.why: Estimate: 3.5 × 3 = 10.5, a bit less. 35 × 26 = 910. 2 decimal places → 9.1.
sets.no: Multiply without the decimal points, then count the decimal places in BOTH factors.

sets.q: Lesson 6 review. The greatest common factor (GCF) of 42 and 70 is ____.
sets.why: Factors of 42: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. Factors of 70: 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, 14, 35, 70. The greatest one in both lists is 14.
sets.no: List the factor pairs of each number. Find the biggest number in BOTH lists.

sets.q: Lesson 3 review. 3/4 + 5/6 = ____ Type it as a mixed number in simplest form.
sets.no: Rename both with a common denominator, add the numerators, then convert the improper fraction to a mixed number.

sets.q: 5/7 = ____/42 Type the missing numerator.
sets.why: 7 × 6 = 42, so multiply the numerator by 6 too: 5 × 6 = 30. 5/7 = 30/42.
sets.no: What do you multiply 7 by to get 42? Multiply the numerator by that same number.

sets.q: Simplify in one step with the GCF: 36/63 = ____
sets.no: Find the greatest common factor of the numerator and the denominator. Divide BOTH by it. Then check: do the new numbers share any factor except 1?

sets.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 6/9?
no: That adds 1 to the top and bottom. Adding changes the amount.
That multiplies the top by 2 and the bottom by 3. Multiply both by the SAME number.
That multiplies only the denominator. Do the same to both.

sets.q: Change it to a mixed number: 37/6 = ____
sets.why: 37 ÷ 6 = 6 R1. The quotient 6 is the whole number. The remainder 1 is the new numerator, and the denominator stays 6. 6 1/6
sets.no: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator, and the denominator stays the same. Type a space between the whole number and the fraction.

sets.q: Change it to an improper fraction: 9 3/4 = ____/4 Type the numerator.
sets.why: 9 wholes = 9 × 4 = 36 fourths. Add the 3 more: 36 + 3 = 39. 9 3/4 = 39/4.
sets.no: Multiply the whole number by the denominator first (9 × 4), then add the numerator. The denominator stays 4.

sets.q: Diego sets 6 border tiles in a row. Each tile is 3/4 foot long. How long is the row? Type a mixed number in simplest form.
sets.why: 6 tiles × 3 fourths = 18 fourths = 18/4. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 R2, so 4 2/4 = 4 1/2 feet.
sets.no: Count the fourths in all (6 × 3), write the improper fraction, convert it, and simplify the fraction part.

sets.q: Which sentence is the topic sentence?

visual.text:
Practice paragraph
Under the Street
(1) Before a new building can open, it must be connected to the pipes under the street. (2) First, a crew digs a deep trench from the building to the street. (3) Next, plumbers lay a water pipe and a sewer pipe in the trench. (4) For example, a large building may need a water pipe as wide as a dinner plate. (5) Finally, the crew fills the trench and patches the road.

choices: (2) First, a crew digs a deep trench from the building to the street.
(5) Finally, the crew fills the trench and patches the road.
(3) Next, plumbers lay a water pipe and a sewer pipe in the trench.
(1) Before a new building can open, it must connect to the pipes.
sets.why: Every other sentence tells a step in connecting the pipes. Sentence 1 tells that main idea.
no: That is the first step, a supporting detail.
That is a step, a supporting detail.

sets.q: Which transition in sentence 4 gives an example? Type it.
sets.why: “For example, a large building may need a water pipe as wide as a dinner plate.” It gives an example of a pipe.
sets.no: Look at the first words of sentence 4.

sets.q: Which sentence is the topic sentence?

visual.text:
Practice paragraph
Keeping Workers Safe
(1) A building site has many rules to keep workers safe. (2) Every worker must wear a hard hat in case something falls. (3) Workers on high floors also wear harnesses that clip to strong ropes. (4) One windy morning, a loose board fell from the fourth floor and hit a worker’s hard hat. (5) As a result of these rules, the worker walked away without a scratch.

choices: (2) Every worker must wear a hard hat.
(1) A building site has many rules to keep workers safe.
(4) One windy morning, a loose board fell from the fourth floor.
(3) Workers on high floors also wear harnesses.
sets.why: Every other sentence is about the safety rules and what they do. Sentence 1 tells that main idea.
no: That is one rule, a supporting detail.
That is part of an example story, a supporting detail.
That is one rule, a supporting detail.

sets.q: Which transition in sentence 5 shows an effect? Type it.
answers: as a result of these rules
sets.why: “As a result of these rules, the worker walked away without a scratch.” Staying safe is the effect of the rules.
sets.no: Look at the first words of sentence 5.
